key_insight: G-Retriever’s graph tokens collapse into nearly input-independent soft prompts, so strong task accuracy does not establish that the LLM uses graph information.
engineering_relevance: Test graph-token dependence with controlled interventions and constant-prompt baselines before attributing performance gains to graph encoding.
method: Analyze token collapse across graph encoders, LLM families, and frozen or LoRA-adapted models.
Replace graph tokens with dataset means, other examples’ tokens, or corrupted-graph tokens; compare against a learned constant prompt.
Evaluate a two-stage procedure for non-collapsed tokens using interventions and decoding probes.
evidence_signal: Across three benchmarks, three graph encoders, and two LLM families, token substitutions produced no resolved answer-accuracy effect under the standard setup, while a learned constant prompt matched or surpassed G-Retriever on every benchmark.
watch_item: The two-stage procedure maintains competitive performance in most cases, but token variability alone does not demonstrate useful graph-information transfer.
paper_title: On the Token Collapse Phenomenon in Textual Graph Soft Prompting
